subject: Runtime variant surface & SDK fallback — cross-functional ask
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martín <elena@finai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Runtime variant surface & SDK fallback — cross-functional ask

Elena — thanks for the heads up in the support ticket. Quick summary for visibility and next steps: FinAI is seeing intermittent tail-latency spikes on our hosted endpoint during heavy ingestion windows (3–5pm ET). When the runtime falls back to the quantized variant under load it sometimes adds a large latency spike for a subset of requests (~600–900ms), which is breaking one of their synchronous flows.

Ask: can we expose a way for a customer to indicate they prefer deterministic variant fallback behavior (either per-request or per-route) so that FinAI can force a graceful, predictable fallback (and not trigger the cold-starty path that lengthens latency unpredictably)? They are also asking for a short SLA exception while we roll a mitigation.

What I’m attaching: runtime_logs_20270404.tar.gz (prod traces), finai_security_qs.xlsx (requested by their procurement).

Things I want from Platform/Runtime:
- A short design option: header-level hint (SDK flag) vs route-level console override, with rough perf implications.
- Miminal ETA estimate to ship an SDK header and server-side route override.
- If we can provide a temporary SLA-exemption / guardrail for FinAI while we roll the change.

If we can get a short triage call today I can bring FinAI and go through their sample prompts.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Runtime variant surface & SDK fallback — cross-functional ask

On Sun, Apr 4, 2027 at 9:12 AM Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com> wrote:
> Elena — thanks for the heads up in the support ticket...

Thanks for the clear write-up, Dylan. A few clarifying q's from runtime/serving: 
1) Does FinAI need the option on a per-request basis (they set a header on each call) or would a per-route override (configured by us in the Console for their tenant) suffice? The perf trade-offs differ.
2) The traces show a spike in cold-starts when we route to fallback-quant variants. Is the tolerance window OK if the first request after a variant switch experiences +200ms, or do they need sub-100ms consistency?

Technical note: switching variants at runtime today can cause a small rewarm of the VM and model artifacts; typical 95p is fine but 99.9p can jump if we evict hot caches. Two immediate options we can offer: 
- Header approach: "Prefer-Variant: fallback-quant" — server will attempt variant selection without a full reload but behavior is best-effort.
- Route override: set the routing policy for FinAI's route to prefer the fallback-quant variant; this avoids per-call negotiation but may increase token-cost.

We should also capture the exact prompt shapes that trigger the worst tails. Can you get their sample prompts and a few example requests? I can look at traces and estimate the rewarm penalty.

I can join a triage call today at 2pm PT.

—Soojin
Soojin Lee
Principal Platform Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Elena Martín <elena@finai.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@finai.com
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 13:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Runtime variant surface & SDK fallback — cross-functional ask

Thanks Dylan and Soojin — appreciate the quick response.

A few clarifications from our side:
- The failures are observed during our batch ingest windows (roughly 3–5pm ET), where a portion of calls that are on synchronous paths bump from ~120ms to ~700–900ms. The flow that breaks is a validation call; we can tolerate up to ~300–350ms but anything above ~500ms causes timeouts in our downstream.
- Per-request header would be easiest for us from an SDK integration perspective, but a route-level override (configured by you) would be workable as a short-term fix.
- I've attached a small sample of the prompts that reproduce the issue: finai_sample_prompts.csv.

On the SLA exception: we need a short-term commitment that you will not apply throttles or non-graceful fallbacks during our scheduled rollout windows next week. If you can provide that in writing we can proceed with the staged rollout.

Happy to take the 2pm PT call.

—Elena
Elena Martín
Head of Integrations, FinAI

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Runtime variant surface & SDK fallback — cross-functional ask

Summary and proposed path forward after looking at the traces and the sample prompts:

Short-term (stopgap, <48h):
- Console route override: we can set an account-scoped routing policy for FinAI to prefer fallback-quant for their route. This is manual but avoids adding SDK changes; Marissa, can you patch the route and confirm no billing impacts?
- Sales to provide a temporary SLA-exemption doc (attached: sla_exemption_finai_20270406.md) to cover their rollout windows. Ops will need Marissa's sign-off.

Medium-term (product lane, 2 sprints):
- Ship a light SDK header: "Prefer-Variant: fallback-quant". Implementation: SDK surface + server-side honor header in routing logic. Expected perf impact: best-effort variant selection; first-call rewarm ~150–250ms in worst cases. We should document this behavior clearly.

Action items / owners:
- Dylan: coordinate triage call and collect any remaining failing request IDs.
- Soojin: estimate rewarm penalty and confirm whether we can implement a less-disruptive warm-path for flavored variants (owner: runtime team).
- Marissa: request Ops for SLA exemption and set up route override temporarily.
- Logan: draft SDK RFC and prioritization note for PM approval.

I’ll book a 60-min working session for tomorrow morning PT; please accept if available.

—Logan
Logan Wright
Product Manager, Redwood Inference
